statusDetail: Coverage complete. Five representative guest paths were audited; authenticated account management, payment, upload, live chat, and completion of legal identity verification were not exercised because they require credentials, personal data, payment, or external verification.

page.notes: Server-rendered, localized media platform with a controlling service worker, manifest, consent layer, and jurisdictional age-verification handoff.

principleOutcomes.reason: The representative guest media-browsing journey has no declared agent-facing capability or on-device inference task; this emerging principle is judged not applicable.

paths.description: Public homepage and main discovery feed. Represents global navigation, consent, age-verification entry, recommendations, and the primary browse journey.
Amateur category listing. Represents category and filtered-list templates.
Representative video detail selected from the homepage. Represents playback metadata, creator context, recommendations, and the legally required age-verification handoff.
Guest registration entry. Represents authentication, form semantics, input assistance, and consent interaction. Registration was inspected but not completed with personal data.
Intentional unknown route. Represents HTTP failure and recovery behavior.

findings.summary: Shimmer animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion evaluate probe found eight running shimmer-56cf2 animations, each with a 2000 ms duration, while prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matched.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential shimmer and auto-motion inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), preserving only state changes that need motion.

findings.summary: High-contrast preference does not produce a distinct high-contrast treatment.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more screenshot retains the standard palette, while the Lighthouse audit independently found text ratios as low as 1.75:1 on the age banner.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-contrast: more treatment and forced-colors-safe borders, text, focus indicators, and scrollbars.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The quality probe found no view-transition signal and sampled navigation swaps pages without a continuity cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-document and cross-document navigation with View Transitions, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The sticky navigation does not react to scroll state.
findings.evidence: The DOM shows a sticky 40 px navigation bar, while the quality probe found no scroll-state or scroll-timeline signal. It remains static as content scrolls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scroll-state container query or a lightweight declarative shrinking-header treatment to reduce persistent chrome.

findings.summary: Consent, age verification, and promotion layers dominate the entry viewport.
findings.evidence: The desktop screenshot shows a central cookie wall obscuring the feed, a full-width age-verification banner, and a promotional strip before the primary content.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep legally required notices concise, preserve equal consent choices, defer promotions, and ensure non-modal notices do not obscure the primary content.

findings.summary: The cookie modal is custom chrome without dialog semantics.
findings.evidence: The screenshot shows a modal interaction, but the DOM probe found zero dialog, role=dialog, or popover elements on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement modal consent with <dialog> or role=dialog plus aria-modal, labelled title, focus containment, Escape behavior, and restoration.

findings.summary: Persistent navigation, sidebars, banners, and ads leave limited room for content.
findings.evidence: The entry screenshot allocates the top 224 px to header and banners and a 230 px left rail before the main grid, with the cookie layer covering the center.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse secondary chrome, defer promotions, and prioritize the feed and current task in the first viewport.

findings.summary: The desktop-width layout is unusable at a 360 px viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout captures on home, category, and video detail report a 1024 px scroll width against a 360 px visual viewport, producing 664 px horizontal overflow. The mobile screenshot shows clipped navigation and content.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove fixed 1024 px page widths, use intrinsic fluid sizing and responsive composition, and verify every template at 320 to 400 px without horizontal scrolling.

findings.summary: Reusable content blocks do not adapt to the available container.
findings.evidence: The quality probe found no container-query signal, and the same 1024 px composition persists inside a 360 px visual viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable rails, cards, and grids containment and size-aware layouts using @container, with intrinsic fallbacks.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch target affordances are inadequate.
findings.evidence: The focused first link computed to outline-style none; the quality probe counted 51 visible targets below 24 px, and Lighthouse failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Add clear :focus-visible indicators and enlarge or space interactive targets to at least the WCAG minimum, preferably about 44 CSS px for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint misses the good threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 3.9 s and FCP at 2.4 s. The independent trace measured LCP at 1.55 s, indicating condition sensitivity rather than a consistently good load.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP element, prioritize its critical resource, reduce startup CSS and script work, and validate under representative mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Startup scripting creates long main-thread tasks.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded two long tasks, with the longest at 198 ms and total blocking time of 168.56 ms; mobile layout sampling also saw tasks up to 219 ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Break startup work into prioritized tasks, defer non-essential modules, and move suitable computation off the main thread.

findings.summary: The load has a large script and request dependency surface.
findings.evidence: The HAR captured 142 requests, 60 scripts, 1.01 MB of transferred script, three parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets, and additional parser-inserted scripts that need deferral review.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce critical CSS, defer or conditionally load non-critical scripts, and explicitly prioritize only true critical resources.

findings.summary: The page ships avoidable unused CSS and JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 57 KiB unused CSS and 26 KiB unused JavaScript on its mobile run, including stylesheets with 87 to 95 percent unused bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Split page-specific CSS and JavaScript, load optional widgets on demand, and remove duplicated or legacy payloads.

findings.summary: Many interactive controls lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse scored accessibility 0.72 and failed button-name and link-name. The independent probe counted one unnamed button and 42 unnamed links in the sampled DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every interactive element a stable accessible name, use native controls, and expose decorative icons as hidden rather than unlabeled controls.

findings.summary: Important age-verification text fails WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured contrast ratios of 2.15:1 and 1.75:1 for text on the green age-verification banner, below the required 4.5:1 for normal text.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose foreground and background colors that meet WCAG AA in all preference modes and verify both standard and high-contrast states.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on sampled navigation.
findings.evidence: After programmatically focusing the first navigation link, computed style reported outline-style none and no box shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply a high-contrast :focus-visible ring that is not clipped, preserve logical tab order, and test the cookie and signup dialogs by keyboard.

findings.summary: Text and navigation are clipped on narrow screens.
findings.evidence: The 360 px screenshot cuts off search, navigation labels, the age-verification copy, and feed content because the layout remains 1024 px wide.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow text and navigation at narrow widths, use intrinsic line wrapping, and avoid fixed-width containers that hide reading content.

findings.summary: The page fails narrow reflow and target sizing.
findings.evidence: At 360 px the layout overflows by 664 px, while Lighthouse separately reports insufficient target size and spacing.
findings.suggestedFix: Meet WCAG reflow at narrow equivalent zoom, retain user scaling, and increase target size and spacing.

findings.summary: Image sizing is inconsistent and risks waste and late layout work.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 29 of 36 images without width and height attributes, 13 oversized images, and one missing alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height or aspect-ratio for every image, select sources close to rendered size, and keep meaningful alternative text.

findings.summary: The video detail lacks structured data.
findings.evidence: The video metadata probe found complete Open Graph and Twitter cards but no JSON-LD on a page representing a VideoObject.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org VideoObject JSON-LD that matches the visible title, creator, thumbnail, duration, upload date, and content policy.

findings.summary: Cookies and the XSS policy are weaker than the secure baseline.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and HSTS are present, but the CSP only contains frame-ancestors. Two first-party cookies lack Secure, and settings uses SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark all HTTPS cookies Secure, use appropriate SameSite and HttpOnly attributes, and deploy a nonce or hash based CSP covering script, style, connect, image, media, and object sources.

findings.summary: A broad third-party and analytics footprint loads before consent.
findings.evidence: The initial HAR recorded 115 of 142 requests and 1.57 MB of 1.68 MB as third-party by origin, including collector, ad, CDN, and Google account endpoints while the consent wall was still visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential analytics, ad, and personalization requests until consent; minimize identifiers; batch allowed analytics; and document essential CDN exceptions.

findings.summary: The signup surface does not expose a passkey path.
findings.evidence: The signup dialog offers Google, X, and email registration, but the sampled auth UI exposes no passkey or WebAuthn option. No permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and authentication alongside federated and recovery options, requested only after user intent.

findings.summary: Defensive response policies are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The headers probe found no X-Content-Type-Options and no Referrer-Policy header; the HTML explicitly declares referrer=unsafe-url. Permissions-Policy is narrowly configured, and CSP only protects framing.
findings.suggestedFix: Set nosniff, a privacy-preserving Referrer-Policy, a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and a comprehensive CSP with Trusted Types where applicable.

findings.summary: The layout is not prepared for alternate writing modes.
findings.evidence: The German document has the correct lang value, but no dir value and the sampled authored style signals contain no logical inline or block properties; the same fixed composition already fails narrow reflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Set direction explicitly where localized templates require it and migrate directional spacing and positioning to logical properties, especially for Arabic, Persian, and Hebrew variants.

findings.summary: German-facing popularity counts use English-style compact formatting.
findings.evidence: The German screenshot shows counts such as 16.2M and 811.1K Aufrufe rather than locale-aware German separators and abbreviations.
findings.suggestedFix: Format counts, dates, numbers, and durations with Intl using the active locale instead of shared English abbreviations.

findings.summary: The email signup step disables useful autofill and lacks a persistent label.
findings.evidence: After selecting email signup, the active control was <input id="email" name="email" placeholder="Email *" autocomplete="off">. The placeholder is not a durable label.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a visible <label>, autocomplete="email", appropriate inputmode and type, and preserve password-manager and paste behavior.

findings.summary: The image payload is not consistently resolution-efficient.
findings.evidence: The images probe found 13 oversized images, 15 legacy-format responses, 29 images without dimensions, and three without responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF or WebP at the actual rendered size, use srcset and sizes consistently, and reserve image geometry.

findings.summary: Startup performs more network and script work than the first view needs.
findings.evidence: The page loads 60 scripts and 142 total requests; Lighthouse found heavily unused CSS and JavaScript, and the trace recorded long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load offscreen and optional widgets, deprioritize background fetches, and remove unused startup code.

findings.summary: Third-party resources dominate the page budget.
findings.evidence: Third-party origins account for about 93 percent of transferred bytes, with 15 third-party origins observed before the user resolves consent.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, defer ad and social modules until needed and permitted, consolidate CDN origins where practical, and cache immutable media aggressively.

taskList.title: Make every template genuinely responsive and reflowable
Gate third-party collection until consent and cut the third-party budget
Restore accessible names, contrast, focus, and target sizing
Strengthen CSP, cookie flags, referrer policy, and browser defenses
Reduce startup scripts, unused code, and long tasks
Reduce entry-page interruptions and use semantic modal primitives
Respect reduced motion and high contrast preferences
Optimize image dimensions, formats, and responsive sources
Improve signup input assistance and add passkeys
Add VideoObject structured data and locale-aware formatting
Add progressive navigation continuity and scroll-aware chrome
